findings: The change is confined to rebuild_dependency_batches=true. The ordinary/public false-branch keeps the previous chunk loop; data before/after that loop and transaction boundaries reconstruct exactly to the fixed parent.

Two lazily initialized Option<CachedStatement> values borrow the same Connection for only this file call. Plain/compressed variants use identical base SQL; FTS has its own fixed SQL. No statement borrows chunk text/blob memory after execute; clear_bindings explicitly matches prior CachedStatement Drop cleanup.

Fallible source_json and compression choice precede base prepare/bind/execute on every row, then conn.last_insert_rowid is evaluated before lazy FTS preparation. Missing FTS and invalid source therefore retain the old visible prefix. Later errors return immediately and drop both handles before caller teardown.

Fixed rusqlite0.40.1 execute binds, checks, steps and resets. New code maps through the same db_err before clearing bindings, including bind/check/step failures, and does not add an extra sqlite reset or change row parameters.

Existing connection cache capacity is unchanged. The two live handles are outside the cache until their file call ends; cache recency/retention differs as intended. This is not a claim of identical allocation or byte-identical binary, and no wall-time gain has yet been measured.

Six added ordinary controls compare the original prepare_cached/drop loop and typed complete database values, including source/short sidecar, empty input/missing FTS/visible prefix, constraint/trigger order/rollback, binding cleanup/failure, schema change/reprepare and public/rebuild values.

The ignored cost probe uses the exact retained original per-row loop baseline, four input classes and20 alternating rounds. It compares full typed base/FTS rows, with begin/readback/rollback outside timer and no speed threshold. This is an in-memory mechanism observation, not full-staging or P8 scale evidence.
limitations: Rust compiler, rustfmt, six controls and ignored probe have not run in this environment. Static review cannot certify compilation or performance.
Existing original study budgets, workload, oracle, task states and source identities are not changed or credited by this review.
